The whey protein peptides-iron chelate had good pH, salt concentration and gastrointestinal digestive stability compared to FeCl2, ferrous gluconate and ferrous glycine. Besides, the DPPH eliminate ability and bacteriostatic properties of the whey protein peptides-iron chelate (WPP-Fe) were better than the whey protein peptide (WPP). These findings can be used as a theoretical basis for the development of new peptide iron supplements. ... The work aimed to assess the antioxidant ability and obtain a new antioxidant peptide from rice bran protein.
Furthermore, absorption inhibitors and enhancers present in the diet can also affect the bioavailability of iron in humans. Diets rich in protein, B complex vitamins and ascorbic acid promote iron storage in the human body, whereas phytic acid, polyphenols, oxalic acid and fiber hinder iron absorption (Bathla and Arora, 2021, Gibson et al., 2018). At present, the intake of iron-fortified foods has become an effective method globally to prevent and improve IDA. Traditional iron supplements include ferrous sulfate, ferrous chloride, and ferrous lactate.
Iron-chelating peptides have been developed and utilized as novel iron supplements, and have been reported to have higher bioavailability with no adverse effects (Caetano-Silva et al., 2021, Guo et al., 2014, Tian et al., 2021). Three transport pathways have been proposed for chelating peptides promoting the absorption of ferrous ions: ferrous ion transport pathway, peptide absorption pathway and peptide as metal ion transport carrier (Caetano-Silva et al., 2021, Tian et al., 2021).
However, these iron supplements have the drawbacks of gastrointestinal irritation, low bioavailability of the body, and strong adverse effects (Hurrell, 2002, Lewis et al., 2017). As an amino acid–chelating agent, ferrous glycinate is 2.5–3.4 times more bioavailable than ferrous sulfate, with minimal gastrointestinal symptoms (Mimura, et al., 2008).
